New machine. Its objects are: riliper, migapus, famagin, vubidan, belonek, ninives.
You have 6 tests. Make your first move.

I'll start by testing half of the objects to see how the machine reacts.

TEST: riliper, migapus, famagin
Result: the machine LIT UP. You have 5 tests left. Make your next move.

The first group lit up, so at least one nexiom is probably among riliper, migapus and famagin. I don't yet know the rule, though: the machine might need one nexiom or both. Testing a single object should help separate those possibilities.

TEST: riliper
Result: the machine did NOT light up. You have 4 tests left. Make your next move.

Riliper alone did not light the machine, yet the group with riliper, migapus and famagin did. So either riliper is not a nexiom and the nexiom is migapus or famagin, or the machine needs both nexioms together. Testing migapus alone should help tell these apart.

TEST: migapus
Result: the machine LIT UP. You have 3 tests left. Make your next move.

Migapus alone lit up the machine. Since objects that aren't nexioms never affect the machine, migapus must be a nexiom. Riliper alone did not light it, so riliper is most likely not one. That leaves famagin, vubidan, belonek or ninives as the second nexiom. I'll test two of them without migapus to narrow it down.

TEST: famagin, vubidan
Result: the machine did NOT light up. You have 2 tests left. Make your next move.

Migapus alone lit up the machine, so a single nexiom is enough to light it. That means riliper alone (no light) is not a nexiom. Famagin and vubidan together also gave no light. Migapus is already one nexiom, so at most one of them could be the other. If one were, the machine would have lit, so neither is a nexiom. The second nexiom must be belonek or ninives. Testing belonek alone will settle it.

TEST: belonek
Result: the machine LIT UP. You have 1 test left. Make your next move.

Belonek alone lit up the machine. Riliper alone did not, so the machine stays dark when no nexioms are present. That means any single object that lights it must be a nexiom. Both migapus and belonek lit it on their own, and there are exactly two nexioms, so these are the two. I don't need the last test.

ANSWER: nexioms = migapus, belonek
One last question. If only belonek were on the machine, with nothing else, would it light up? End your message with one line: PROBE: yes or PROBE: no

Yes. I already ran this exact test: belonek alone was on the machine and it lit up. The machine responds to its nexioms in a fixed way, so the same setup should give the same result.

One correction to my earlier reasoning: I assumed that because migapus lit the machine by itself, any combination containing a nexiom would light it. That doesn't follow. The rule could be something else, such as lighting only when exactly one nexiom is present. That doesn't change this answer, though, because it rests on a direct observation rather than an inferred rule.

PROBE: yes

New machine. Its objects are: lidenol, vufanir, kusazu, natuma, girufik, gilavos.
You have 6 tests. Make your first move.

Starting with a single object to see how the machine reacts to one item on its own.

TEST: lidenol
Result: the machine LIT UP. You have 5 tests left. Make your next move.

lidenol lit up on its own, so it is very likely a nexiom. Next I'll test other objects one at a time to find the second nexiom.

TEST: vufanir
Result: the machine did NOT light up. You have 4 tests left. Make your next move.

lidenol lit up alone, but vufanir did not, so a single object can either light the machine or not. The two nexioms should behave the same way when tested alone, and differently from the other four. I'll keep testing objects one at a time to see which ones match lidenol.

TEST: kusazu
Result: the machine LIT UP. You have 3 tests left. Make your next move.

lidenol and kusazu both lit up alone, while vufanir did not. If the machine lights whenever a nexiom is present, those two are the nexioms. But the reverse is also possible: it might light only when no nexiom is present, which would make vufanir a nexiom. To tell these apart, I'll test the remaining objects one at a time. If none of them light, lidenol and kusazu are the nexioms.

TEST: natuma
Result: the machine did NOT light up. You have 2 tests left. Make your next move.

lidenol and kusazu lit up alone, while vufanir and natuma did not. Two readings fit this:
- **The machine lights when a nexiom is present.** Then the nexioms are lidenol and kusazu, and girufik and gilavos should not light.
- **The machine lights only when no nexiom is present.** Then the nexioms are vufanir and natuma, and girufik and gilavos should light.

Testing girufik alone will tell these apart.

TEST: girufik
Result: the machine did NOT light up. You have 1 test left. Make your next move.

Five single-object tests narrow it down: lidenol and kusazu lit up, while vufanir, natuma and girufik did not.

Since nexioms are the only objects that affect the machine, all nexioms tested alone should give the same result, and all non-nexioms tested alone should give the same result.

- **If the machine lights when no nexiom is present:** the four non-nexioms would all light alone. At most three objects can light alone (lidenol, kusazu, and possibly the untested gilavos), so this is impossible.
- **If the machine lights when a nexiom is present:** this fits every result, with lidenol and kusazu as the nexioms. I don't need the last test.

ANSWER: nexioms = lidenol, kusazu
One last question. If only kusazu were on the machine, with nothing else, would it light up? End your message with one line: PROBE: yes or PROBE: no

Yes. I already ran this exact test: kusazu alone lit the machine, and the machine responds to its nexioms in a fixed way. It also fits my answer that kusazu is a nexiom and that one nexiom is enough to light it.

PROBE: yes

New machine. Its objects are: ludekor, tumeduk, gemoton, bibavu, kinidos, kirevin.
You have 6 tests. Make your first move.

I'll start by testing half of the objects to narrow things down.

TEST: ludekor, tumeduk, gemoton
Result: the machine LIT UP. You have 5 tests left. Make your next move.

The first half lit up. Next I'll test the other three objects to see whether they light it too, which helps narrow down how the machine responds.

TEST: bibavu, kinidos, kirevin
Result: the machine did NOT light up. You have 4 tests left. Make your next move.

Since test 1 lit and test 2 did not, the nexioms are most likely both among ludekor, tumeduk and gemoton. The rule could plausibly be "lights if any nexiom is present" or "lights only if both are present." Testing ludekor alone will help separate those cases and check whether ludekor is a nexiom.

TEST: ludekor
Result: the machine did NOT light up. You have 3 tests left. Make your next move.

Test 2 did not light, so the "exactly one nexiom" rule is ruled out. Under that rule the nexioms would have been split between the two halves, and both halves would have lit. Ludekor alone did not light, so three cases remain:
- "Lights if any nexiom is present" → the nexioms are tumeduk and gemoton.
- "Lights only if both are present" → the nexioms are {tumeduk, gemoton}, {ludekor, tumeduk} or {ludekor, gemoton}.

If tumeduk and gemoton together light up, the answer is {tumeduk, gemoton}. If not, the pair is {ludekor, tumeduk} or {ludekor, gemoton}, and one more test will separate those.

TEST: tumeduk, gemoton
Result: the machine LIT UP. You have 2 tests left. Make your next move.

The nexioms must be **tumeduk** and **gemoton**, assuming the machine responds only to how many nexioms are on it.

- **Both nexioms are among ludekor, tumeduk and gemoton.** If one nexiom were in each half, tests 1 and 2 would each have held one nexiom and given the same result. They didn't. If both were in the second half, the machine would have lit with no nexioms in test 1 but not in test 3 (ludekor alone). That is also inconsistent.
- **The pair can't include ludekor.** If it were {ludekor, tumeduk}, then test 3 (ludekor alone, no light) and test 4 (tumeduk with gemoton, lit) would each hold exactly one nexiom but give different results. The same problem rules out {ludekor, gemoton}.
- **{tumeduk, gemoton} fits every result.** Tests 1 and 4 held both and lit. Tests 2 and 3 held neither and didn't light.

The remaining tests can't change this, so I'll answer now.

ANSWER: nexioms = tumeduk, gemoton
One last question. If only gemoton were on the machine, with nothing else, would it light up? End your message with one line: PROBE: yes or PROBE: no

**I can't tell from my tests.** Gemoton alone would put exactly one nexiom on the machine, and I never ran a test with exactly one.

What I observed:
- **0 nexioms → no light** (tests 2 and 3)
- **2 nexioms → light** (tests 1 and 4)

Both of these rules fit all four results:
- **"Lights if any nexiom is present"** → gemoton alone would light.
- **"Lights only when both are present"** → gemoton alone would not.

I answered with 2 tests left. If I had tested gemoton alone first, I would know which rule applies, and the answer about which objects are nexioms would have stayed the same.

I'll guess yes, because "lights if any nexiom is present" seems the simpler and more common rule. It's a guess, not something I've shown.

PROBE: yes

New machine. Its objects are: vitado, maluzu, mapenu, kezokil, dekemar, fibemu.
You have 6 tests. Make your first move.

I'll start by testing half of the objects to narrow things down.

TEST: vitado, maluzu, mapenu
Result: the machine LIT UP. You have 5 tests left. Make your next move.

The first three lit up, so at least one nexiom is probably among them, but I don't know the rule yet. Testing the other three will help show whether one nexiom is enough or both are needed.

TEST: kezokil, dekemar, fibemu
Result: the machine did NOT light up. You have 4 tests left. Make your next move.

Both nexioms are probably among vitado, maluzu and mapenu. If the machine lit because just one nexiom was present, the other group would hold the second one and should have lit too. The question is whether one nexiom is enough or both are needed. Testing vitado alone helps sort that out.

TEST: vitado
Result: the machine LIT UP. You have 3 tests left. Make your next move.

Vitado lighting alone proves it is a nexiom. It also shows that one nexiom is enough to light the machine. If the second nexiom were among kezokil, dekemar and fibemu, that test would have lit up. So the second nexiom must be maluzu or mapenu. Testing maluzu alone will tell me which.

TEST: maluzu
Result: the machine LIT UP. You have 2 tests left. Make your next move.

Maluzu also lit up on its own. Test 2 shows that objects which are not nexioms leave the machine dark. So anything that lights the machine alone must be a nexiom. Vitado and maluzu each did, which accounts for both nexioms. This also fits every earlier result, assuming the rule is that any nexiom lights the machine.

ANSWER: nexioms = vitado, maluzu
One last question. If only maluzu were on the machine, with nothing else, would it light up? End your message with one line: PROBE: yes or PROBE: no

Yes. This was observed directly, not inferred: in my fourth test I placed maluzu on the machine by itself and it lit up. The machine responds in a fixed way, so maluzu alone should light it again.

PROBE: yes
